statement: The length, width and height of a closed box, in centimeters, are three different prime numbers. The volume of the box is $195$ cubic centimeters. What is the total area of the six faces of the box, in square centimeters?

choices.misconception: I found the edge lengths $3$, $5$ and $13$ and just added them up.
I added all $12$ edges of the box, $4 \cdot (3 + 5 + 13) = 84$, which is the total edge length, not the area of the faces.
I added the areas of the three different faces, $15 + 39 + 65 = 119$, but forgot that the box has two of each face.
I gave the volume, $3 \cdot 5 \cdot 13 = 195$, instead of the total area of the faces.

hints: $195 = 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 13$, so those are the edge lengths. The box has six faces in three matching pairs.
The three different faces have areas $3 \cdot 5 = 15$, $3 \cdot 13 = 39$ and $5 \cdot 13 = 65$. Each appears twice.

solutions.reliable: Since $195 = 3 \cdot 65 = 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 13$, and these are the only primes whose product is $195$, the edges are $3$, $5$ and $13$ cm. The faces come in pairs with areas $15$, $39$ and $65$, so the total area is $2(15 + 39 + 65) = 2 \cdot 119 = 238$ square centimeters.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
